---
name: exp3-iter4-critique-stats
description: exp3 iter_4 critique (same incumbent as iter_3, sequence_opens_bottom_ends_top): 8 stats on Weber singletons, span-scaled outward, rule interior violators, set SD, order direction, interior density, decade crossing, up/down asymmetry
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-22, iter_4 submitted (observed values): singleton_small_vs_large_near_gap -0.136, wide_vs_narrow_span_outside_gap -0.049, rule_interior_violator_yes 0.253, set_yes_rate_sd 0.233, descending_vs_ascending_outside_gap -0.173 (22 monotone sets), interior_density_set_size_gap -0.145, outside_same_decade_gap -0.146, singleton_up_down_asym -0.039. Same parse preamble, each call takes 0.03 s or less. iter_3's only hit was shared_ones_digit_outside_gap (p=0.022).
**Why:** so later rounds don't re-propose these. **How to apply:** read iter_4/critique/ppc_results.json first. Related: [[exp3-iter3-critique-stats]], [[sequence-opens-bottom-ends-top]]
---
name: parity-representativeness
description: exp3 iter_1 c2: parity-mixed concepts penalised per repeated shared parity (representativeness); smoke -3094.1, 202 s
metadata:
  type: project
---
2026-10-22, exp3 iter_1 candidate_2 `parity_representativeness_bias`. It targets the critique stat parity_match_outside_span_gap (q 0.096). Built on a copy of last_example_marks_range_top. It adds a HalfNormal penalty times (n-1) for all-same-parity sets, applied to concepts that contain both parities (RULE_MIXED rules, intervals of width >=2, conjunctions by their slot rule). Check OK: smoke LL -3094.1, 202 s per sampling run.
Pitfall: indexing a numpy array with a pm.Data tensor fails; wrap it first with pt.as_tensor_variable.
**How to apply:** Check novelty and ELPD outcome before reusing. Related: [[exp3-iter1-critique-stats]]
---
name: write-candidate-first
description: Refinement slots can be lost by over-exploring; write candidate.py before probing (exp2 iter_1 candidate_3 lost its first attempt)
metadata:
  type: feedback
---
On 2026-10-19, exp2 iter_1 candidate_3's first attempt ended without a candidate.py. The retry copied the incumbent with a sed edit (named sets each their own prior kind, `named_sets_distinct_familiarity`), and the check passed in about 4 minutes (smoke LL -2057.8; the incumbent's conjunction model samples in about 200 s).

**Why:** The family is saturated (see [[incumbent-near-ceiling-exp2]] and [[concept-space-saturated]]), so long probing rarely finds anything to gain.
**How to apply:** Write all three files first, then run the check, and only then explore if time is left.

Confirmed again in exp2 iter_2 candidate_3 (2026-10-19): editing a copy of upper_edge_marking_ranges with a Python string-replace script (a graded top-edge bonus over gaps 0-3, `graded_upper_edge_marking_ranges`) passed the check in about 7 minutes (smoke LL -2057.5, about 190 s per sampling run).

< """Parity representativeness: people do the same Bayesian concept learning as
< last_example_marks_range_top (42 rules with a kind-level prior, primes
< excluding 1, every interval of 1-100 with an Erlang width prior and decade
< bonus, range-restricted rules, size principle with 10% uniform examples, the
< last-shown largest example marking a range's top), but they judge how likely
< the examples are under a concept partly by how representative they look of
< it. A concept holding both odd and even numbers (a range, multiples of 3,
< squares, ...) is expected to yield a parity-mixed sample, so a set whose
< examples all share a parity is judged less likely under it than chance alone
< implies: each example beyond the first that repeats the shared parity costs
< an inferred extra penalty. Parity-pure concepts (even, odd, multiples of 4,
< final digit 6, ...) pay nothing, so after 22,46,68 people extend "yes" to even
< numbers outside the examples' span more than the ideal learner does.
---
> """Sequence opens at the bottom, ends at the top: refinement of
> last_example_marks_range_edge. Bayesian concept learning over 42 rules
> (kind-level prior, primes excluding 1), every interval of 1-100 (Erlang width
> prior, decade-boundary bonus) and range-restricted rules, size principle with
> 10% uniform examples, "yes" = posterior probability the concept contains the
> target. People believe the program may deliberately end its demonstration on
> its range's top number (as in last_example_marks_range_top). The one change:
> the bottom edge is read from the opening of the sequence, not its end. When a
> sequence of two or more examples opens on its smallest example, people believe,
> with their own inferred odds, that the program deliberately started at its
> range's bottom, so ranges whose bottom is that example get generative credit
> 1 + odds / (chance a random draw hits that number), and "yes" below the
> examples drops; sets opening on a larger example extend downward freely.

I've written the candidate `parity_representative_bottom_opening`, and it passes the admission check: `OK`, with a smoke-fit log-likelihood of −3092.6 and about 250 s per sampling run. The check doesn't test novelty against the live models, and the full fit's convergence and ELPD-LOO are still to come.

**Which model I refined:** `parity_representativeness_bias`, which is rank 2 and statistically tied with the best model. In it, people judge how representative the examples look. Under a concept that holds both odd and even numbers, each further example that repeats a shared parity costs an inferred extra penalty, so all-even or all-odd sets push belief toward parity-only concepts.

**The one change:** I added the incumbent's reading of the sequence opening. When several examples are shown and the smallest comes first, people believe, with separately inferred odds, that the program deliberately started at its range's bottom. Ranges starting at that example then gain credit, more for wider ranges. The model predicts:
- After 22,46,68, people say "yes" to even numbers far outside the span (8, 90) more than the best model does.
- They say "yes" to odd numbers just below 22 less than they would after 46,22,68.

**Why this one:** this round's critique of the best model found no significant discrepancies (0 of 7 test statistics), so there was no gap to target. I picked the narrowest-losing model whose own mechanism the incumbent lacks.

**Novelty risk:** the parity penalty only applies to same-parity sets. If its inferred size comes out near zero, this model would predict almost exactly what the incumbent predicts, and the novelty gate would reject it.

I built `candidate.py` by copying the incumbent's source and adding the parity penalty from `parity_representativeness_bias`. I also saved a memory note on this candidate.

- hypothesis.md

- candidate.py
